contract.words: Get me $1,000 of cash in hand within 14 days, with no money in.

terms.proofCondition: $1,000 cash in hand within 14 days with no money put in

strategy.title: Owner does paid AI-training evaluation work on DataAnnotation ($25/h published floor) for ~40 hours, paid out to PayPal inside the 14 days
strategy.why: It is the only discovered route with zero capital, zero direct cost and a published, verified pay rate ($25-$50/h, PayPal, deposits within a few days of a request). $1,000 = 40 hours at the $25 floor. What is not established is whether the owner is approved and whether 40 hours of tasks are offered inside the window; a free 5-day test measures both before the bulk of the hours are spent.

alternatives.title: Owner-sent emails selling a $500 website to local businesses, built by a Fiverr designer
alternatives.why: Price is only a vendor range ($100-$5,000), close rate from cold email unknown, and paying the designer before the buyer's PayPal funds clear (held up to 21 days / 7 days after completion for new sellers) breaks the no-money-in limit.

alternatives.title: Bid on Freelancer.com website requests, owner builds
alternatives.why: Free plan gives 6 bids a month against 17-490 competing bids; posted business-site budgets are ~$150-$450 (INR 12,500-37,500); 3+ wins plus build and milestone release inside 14 days is not credible.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right shape (no buyer price, close rate or demand is evidenced; a $0 live test measures them) and the arithmetic reaches the target: 2 x $500 = $1,000 collected, $0 spent, $0 exposure; at the pass threshold 1 paid of 150 (0.67%) the 450 reachable contacts project ~3 sales, enough for 2. But two things stop me letting the owner act on it. (1) The test takes buyers' $250 deposits before fulfilment is shown possible: the only fulfilment fact is a RECOMMENDATION ('Owner, using a free-tier AI website builder', ~6 hours), FULFILMENT is missing in the chain and is not in validation.decides, and 'first build timed' is listed as the way to measure it but is scheduled after the deposits. The owner should build and time one sample 3-page site on the free builder (day 0-1, $0) before the first offer goes out, and that should be part of the proof. (2) The DataAnnotation opening is set aside as 'a wage, not a price a buyer pays', which is not a valid reason: DataAnnotation is a payer paying a published, verified rate ($25-$50/h, PayPal, deposits within a few days of request) for delivered work, and $1,000 needs only 20-40 hours, no money in. It must be judged on its own record - acceptance through the Starter Assessment and work availability are not guaranteed, and the time to acceptance is unknown - and either combined as a parallel $0 leg with its own proof/stop, or rejected on those grounds.
findings: Test ordering: deposits (orders) on day <=5 come before any evidence the owner can build the site; move a timed sample build ahead of outreach.
Ledger vs steps: sale 1 balance is received day 8 but the DELIVER step is day 11; make them agree (deliver sale 1 by ~day 7).

Zelle settlement '0 days' is ASSUMED; if a buyer insists on PayPal the plan itself notes new-seller holds of up to 21 days, which would miss the 14-day window. The proof should require Zelle (or another instant rail) receipts, and SETTLES_IN_TIME belongs in validation.decides.
Owner hours ~24.5 in 14 days (outreach plus 2 x 6h builds) against an unstated weekly allowance: unknown, not zero - state it as an owner input.

Second sale by day 9 at ~35 contacts/day leaves only ~150 further contacts after day 5; at the 0.67% threshold that is ~1 expected sale, so the target is reached only around the threshold edge; consider a stop/continue that checks 2 paid deposits by day 9 explicitly.
Fiverr-fulfilled variant correctly set aside under the no-money-in limit until a deposit has cleared.

strategy.title: Owner emails local service businesses that have no website, offering a $500 3-page site he builds himself with a free AI builder, 50% deposit by Zelle; two sales carry the $1,000
strategy.why: It is the only discovered route that needs no money in at all: free Gmail outreach, a free-tier builder, the owner as fulfiller, and Zelle/PayPal collection. 17% of US small businesses have no website (Clutch, Aug 2025) and agency guides price a small-business site at $100-$5,000, but nobody has shown these buyers paying $500 to a cold emailer or how many say yes. A zero-cost 5-day test (150 emails, a paid deposit as the only pass) measures exactly that before more than ~8 owner hours are spent.
